# AI coding research brief — October 2, 2026

Historical backfill published October 17, 2026. Reconstructed from recovered prior-conversation findings; this is not a verbatim transcript. The original selections, reported results, caveats, and proposed experiments are preserved in condensed form. Dates below are publication dates recorded in the original brief. These are research proposals, not demonstrated Quadratus improvements or implementation instructions.

## 1. Beyond the Model: Demystifying Harness Effects in Software Engineering Agents
**September 26, 2026 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32459)**

Structured tools and task-specific subagents provided the most consistent component gains. The combined NanoHarness improved ProgramBench scores by 7.37 and 6.21 percentage points for Qwen3.7-Max and DeepSeek-V4-Pro respectively. Context compression and general-purpose subagents could hurt repository generation.

**Why read it and limitations:** One universal orchestration policy may waste effort on bounded repairs while underserving repository construction. The study centers on Qwen and DeepSeek; component analysis concentrates on ProgramBench, limiting transfer to other models and tasks.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Compare a lean repair profile and a specialist repository-build profile against the universal workflow on randomized tasks. Track pass rate, omissions, cost and latency.

## 2. Zero2Repo: Can Coding Agents Build Repositories from Scratch?
**September 29, 2026; revised October 1 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38269)**

The earlier brief reported that the strongest agent solved 10 of 11 tasks. Failed submissions often passed 90–99% of tests; 67–100% of the strongest-agent failures were attributed to one omission or an infrequent rule.

**Why read it and limitations:** High partial scores can conceal a missing requirement that prevents completion. The benchmark has only 11 tasks, possible training exposure, and no direct measure of maintainability or architectural quality.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Build an acceptance matrix with an owner for every obligation and test. Require implementation and execution evidence for each obligation before accepting completion.

**Source status:** Preserved from the earlier brief; the source could not be independently reopened during this backfill. Treat the reported results as awaiting source re-verification.

## 3. From Verification Failures to Reusable Guidance for Coding Agents
**September 30, 2026; revised October 1 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39022)**

The earlier brief described executable K semantics, specification construction, proof repair and adequacy auditing. A human-guided HumanEval study reached 164/164 final AI-audit passes after two targeted repairs. Audits distinguished 12 clean packages from deliberately defective counterparts despite passing proofs; results on 31 unfamiliar-semantics programs were mixed.

**Why read it and limitations:** Proving a specification is distinct from establishing that it captures the request. The headline is human-guided and AI-audited, the defect-pair sample is small, and the method requires substantial formal-semantics infrastructure.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Separate contract/test satisfaction from specification-coverage review. Give an independent auditor the original request and acceptance matrix without the implementer's rationale.

**Source status:** Preserved from the earlier brief; the source could not be independently reopened during this backfill. Treat the reported results as awaiting source re-verification.

## 4. Coding Agents for Coding Theory
**September 30, 2026 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39081)**

The earlier brief reported a five-week Claude Code project that improved 13 published lower bounds with independently verified artifacts. An underpowered intermediate result remained treated as settled for three weeks; a fresh session using a better search operator found the missed result.

**Why read it and limitations:** Long-lived conclusions can preserve an earlier search failure as supposed knowledge. This is one domain-specific, human-directed case study with one agent setup; broader orchestration lessons are inferences.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Store provenance and confidence with reusable conclusions. Expire negative claims unless budgets, seeds, tool versions and calibration are recorded. Periodically give a fresh worker the artifacts without inherited conclusions to challenge stopping decisions.

**Source status:** Preserved from the earlier brief; the source could not be independently reopened during this backfill. Treat the reported results as awaiting source re-verification.

## The single most promising idea to try

Replace universal fan-out with task-dependent harness profiles: lean repair and specialist repository-build modes. Preserve acceptance matrices and require independent review of whether the specification covers the request. Compare verified completion, cost and latency before adopting a profile.
